title: nixpkgs-multiverse: every version that ever existed
excerpt: Enter the Nixpkgs multiverse. All the versions that ever existed, all in one place.
content_html:
Enter the Nixpkgs multiverse. All the versions that ever existed, all in one place.

I bumped the nixpkgs release for my NixOS configuration to refresh many of my packages and found that a package I depended on at a particular version is no longer available.

The package was “version bumped forward” in a way that broke some of my tooling. It’s late and I don’t want to fix it, so I just add another nixpkgs input pinned to the commit that had the version I want. This works, but it is miserable in a way that compounds.

{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs-unstable.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    nixpkgs-25_11.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-25.11";
    nixpkgs-25_05.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-25.05";
  };
}

The need for the most recent package is so common that I had keep an overlay that would inject unstable as a package set for me to easily pull from.

unstable-packages = final: _prev: {
  unstable = import inputs.nixpkgs-unstable {
    system = final.stdenv.hostPlatform.system;
    config.allowUnfree = true;
    overlays = [inputs.nix-vscode-extensions.overlays.default];
  };
};

If I have a need for a particular version of a package and it’s not present in my current nixpkgs, I am left searching for the commit and pinning it.11Thankfully sites like nixhub.io or lazamar’s search make this a little easier. 

Every pin is a whole extra nixpkgs in the file. Flake inputs are fetched eagerly even if not used. A flake with three nixpkgs inputs whose output references only the first are all materialised.

Nix lets us easily create a closure that reproduces a specific version of a package, but Nixpkgs makes it hard to hold one package still while everything else moves.

Each Nixpkgs input to a flake is a distinct universe. If we can have multiple Nixpkgs as input to achieve fetching a particular package, why not have every version that ever existed always available? 🤯

nixpkgs-multiverse is one flake input that gives you all of them at once.

$ nix run 'github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#versions.python3."3.6.2"' -- --version
Python 3.6.2

$ nix run 'github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#versions.python3."3.8.9"' -- --version
Python 3.8.9

# We can also get the latest version of a package.
$ nix run 'github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#latest.python3' -- --version
Python 3.14.6

We can query the flake for all the versions of a package that ever existed in Nixpkgs.

$ nix eval --json --apply 'f: f "python3"' \
   github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#multiverse.x86_64-linux.versionsOf
[
  "3.5.3",
  "3.6.2",
  # 53 other versions omitted for brevity
  # ... 
  "3.13.13",
  "3.14.6"
]

If we want a specific complete revision of Nixpkgs we can use the at function.

let
  mv = multiverse.multiverse.x86_64-linux;
  # newest revision the index knows, as a real Nixpkgs
  pkgs_tip = mv.tip;
  # by release
  pkgs_24_11 = mv.at "24.11";
  # newest revision on or before that date
  pkgs_2022_03_15 = mv.at "2022-03-15";
  # by commit
  pkgs_aae12a743f75 = mv.at "aae12a743f75";
in {
  packages = [
      pkgs_tip.python3
      pkgs_24_11.python3
      pkgs_2022_03_15.python3
      pkgs_aae12a743f75.python3
    ];
}

That is access to all the versions of all the packages that ever existed in Nixpkgs. You can mix them all together in one shell, one package or a build environment.

How is it possible to have multiple Python versions? That is the whole point of Nix itself. Every package immaculately describes its dependencies using a hash via the intensional model.22The hash is a unique identifier for the exact set of inputs that were used to build it. If you change any input, the hash changes and you get a new package. 

Nixpkgs already supports multiple versions of a package in a single revision (i.e. python39, python312, gcc12) as separate attributes. We took this to its logical conclusion of making them all available easily.

§What’s the magic?

Our flake.nix deliberately has no inputs: inputs = { }. Inputs are fetched eagerly, and we have 1,393 of them. We need to fetch them lazily, only when something actually references a revision. To do this, we fetch revisions with builtins.fetchTree, pinned by narHash, only when needed.

Two files do all the work: revisions.json and versions.json.

revisions.json is one ordered array of every revision from Nixpkgs, 1,393 as of this writing, from 2017 to 2026.33A NixOS release is not special; it is a commit that happens to carry a release label. 

[
  {
    "rev": "0eeebd64de89…",
    "date": "2023-06-12",
    "channel": "nixos-unstable",
    "narHash": "sha256-2xT+Jmk3m…"
  },
  {
    "rev": "afb2b21ba489…",
    "date": "2025-05-23",
    "channel": "release",
    "release": "25.05",
    "narHash": "sha256-rWtXrcIzU5wm…"
  }
]

We limit our commits to those that were actually built and cached by Hydra, so we only include commits that were either a release or a nixos-unstable channel bump.

How do we know which revisions to pick for the nixos-unstable ones?

We rely on the nix-releases S3 bucket to tell us which commits actually became published builds. The S3 bucket uses the commit hash as the directory name, so we can list the bucket and get a complete list of all revisions that were actually built.

index/versions.json is the map from (attribute, version) to a revision:

{
  "revisionCount": 1393,
  "attrs": {
    "python3": { "3.8.9": 412, "3.12.10": 1204 }
  }
}

That integer is an offset into revisions.json. It is the most recent revision that shipped that version.

§Sparse data

At this many revisions, it turns out that how you encode the data matters a lot. My first encoding stored every revision a version appeared in.

Although it was simple, it was a disaster in terms of size for these JSON files. As you might expect, most versions of most packages are unchanged across many revisions. The size of our versions.json file was growing linearly with the number of revisions.

By storing only the newest revision that shipped a version, we can keep the file small and still answer the question “which revision had this version”. Here is how it actually grows as revisions get indexed:

5.18 MB covering 1,393 revisions and 289,521 distinct (attribute, version) pairs.

§Performance

The key design rule for our flake:

Cost is per revision touched, not per package.

If we were to add revisions as inputs, evaluating our flake would explode. Each flake in our measurement below has N nixpkgs inputs and an output that references only the first one; the timing is how long before that output evaluates.44Everything is git+file against a local clone, so there is no network latency. 

Five nixpkgs pins that are not used cost 26 seconds before the output evaluates. Each input costs about 5 seconds, and the input is fetched and materialised even if never used. In contrast, the green line is nixpkgs-multiverse with 1,393 revisions available, which is a flat 0.20s to parse the JSON. 🤩

Revisions are memoised, so pulling 3 packages out of one revision costs the same as pulling one.

§Why I like this

That concept that the /nix/store can hold many graphs of the same package is core to understanding Nix. The popularity and rise of flakes made it even more apparent that we can mix multiple revisions of Nixpkgs together.

The thing I keep coming back to is that Nixpkgs history already is the multiverse. Every version that ever existed is already built, already cached, already reachable. It was just addressed by commit hash instead of by version number, which is exactly backwards from how anyone thinks about it.

The whole project is 5 MB of JSON and about 200 lines of Nix. It does not build anything, mirror anything, or host anything. It is a phone book.

content_html_zh:
进入 Nixpkgs 多元宇宙。 曾经存在的所有版本都集中在一处。

我为我的 NixOS 配置升级了 nixpkgs 版本以刷新我的许多软件包，并发现我在特定版本上依赖的软件包不再可用。

该软件包的“版本向前推进”在某种程度上破坏了我的一些工具。 已经晚了，我不想修复它，所以我只是添加另一个固定到具有我想要的版本的提交的 nixpkgs 输入。 这确实有效，但在某种程度上却是令人痛苦的。

{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs-unstable.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    nixpkgs-25_11.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-25.11";
    nixpkgs-25_05.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-25.05";
  };
}

对最新软件包的需求是如此普遍，以至于我保留了一个覆盖层，它将注入不稳定的软件包作为我可以轻松提取的软件包集。

unstable-packages = final: _prev: {
  unstable = import inputs.nixpkgs-unstable {
    system = final.stdenv.hostPlatform.system;
    config.allowUnfree = true;
    overlays = [inputs.nix-vscode-extensions.overlays.default];
  };
};

如果我需要某个特定版本的包，并且它不存在于我当前的 nixpkg 中，那么我只能搜索提交并固定它。11值得庆幸的是，像 nixhub.io 或 lazamar 的搜索这样的网站使这变得更容易一些。

文件中的每个引脚都是一个额外的 nixpkgs。 即使不使用薄片输入，也会立即获取。 具有三个 nixpkgs 输入的 flake，其输出仅引用第一个输入，全部实现。

Nix 让我们可以轻松地创建一个可以重现特定版本包的闭包，但是 Nixpkgs 使得在其他所有东西都移动时保持一个包静止变得很困难。

每个 Nixpkgs 输入到一个 flake 都是一个独特的宇宙。 如果我们可以有多个 Nixpkg 作为输入来实现获取特定包，为什么不让曾经存在的每个版本都始终可用呢？ 🤯

nixpkgs-multiverse 是一种片状输入，可以一次为您提供所有这些输入。

$ nix run 'github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#versions.python3."3.6.2"' -- --version
Python 3.6.2

$ nix run 'github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#versions.python3."3.8.9"' -- --version
Python 3.8.9

# We can also get the latest version of a package.
$ nix run 'github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#latest.python3' -- --version
Python 3.14.6

我们可以在 flake 中查询 Nixpkgs 中曾经存在的软件包的所有版本。

$ nix eval --json --apply 'f: f "python3"' \
   github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse#multiverse.x86_64-linux.versionsOf
[
  "3.5.3",
  "3.6.2",
  # 53 other versions omitted for brevity
  # ... 
  "3.13.13",
  "3.14.6"
]

如果我们想要 Nixpkgs 的特定完整修订版，我们可以使用 at 函数。

let
  mv = multiverse.multiverse.x86_64-linux;
  # newest revision the index knows, as a real Nixpkgs
  pkgs_tip = mv.tip;
  # by release
  pkgs_24_11 = mv.at "24.11";
  # newest revision on or before that date
  pkgs_2022_03_15 = mv.at "2022-03-15";
  # by commit
  pkgs_aae12a743f75 = mv.at "aae12a743f75";
in {
  packages = [
      pkgs_tip.python3
      pkgs_24_11.python3
      pkgs_2022_03_15.python3
      pkgs_aae12a743f75.python3
    ];
}

这是对 Nixpkgs 中曾经存在的所有软件包的所有版本的访问。 您可以将它们全部混合在一个 shell、一个包或一个构建环境中。

怎么可能有多个Python版本呢？ 这就是 Nix 本身的全部意义所在。 每个包都通过内涵模型使用哈希完美地描述了其依赖关系。22哈希是用于构建它的确切输入集的唯一标识符。 如果您更改任何输入，哈希值就会更改，并且您会得到一个新包。

Nixpkgs 已经支持单个修订版中包的多个版本（即 python39、python312、gcc12）作为单独的属性。 我们得出了一个合乎逻辑的结论：让它们都可以轻松使用。

§有什么魔力？

我们的 flake.nix 故意没有输入：inputs = { }。 输入被急切地获取，我们有 1,393 个输入。 仅当某些内容实际引用修订版时，我们才需要延迟获取它们。 为此，我们仅在需要时使用由 narHash 固定的builtins.fetchTree 获取修订版本。

两个文件完成所有工作：revisions.json 和 versions.json。

revisions.json 是 Nixpkgs 的每个修订版的有序数组，截至撰写本文时，从 2017 年到 2026 年有 1,393 个修订版。33A NixOS 版本并不特殊；这是一个碰巧带有发布标签的提交。

[
  {
    "rev": "0eeebd64de89…",
    "date": "2023-06-12",
    "channel": "nixos-unstable",
    "narHash": "sha256-2xT+Jmk3m…"
  },
  {
    "rev": "afb2b21ba489…",
    "date": "2025-05-23",
    "channel": "release",
    "release": "25.05",
    "narHash": "sha256-rWtXrcIzU5wm…"
  }
]

我们将提交限制为由 Hydra 实际构建和缓存的提交，因此我们只包含发布版本或 nixos 不稳定通道碰撞的提交。

我们如何知道为 nixos 不稳定的版本选择哪些版本？

我们依靠 nix-releases S3 存储桶来告诉我们哪些提交实际上成为了已发布的版本。 S3 存储桶使用提交哈希作为目录名称，因此我们可以列出该存储桶并获取实际构建的所有修订的完整列表。

index/versions.json 是从（属性，版本）到修订版的映射：

{
  "revisionCount": 1393,
  "attrs": {
    "python3": { "3.8.9": 412, "3.12.10": 1204 }
  }
}

该整数是 revisions.json 中的偏移量。 这是发布该版本的最新修订版。

§稀疏数据

经过如此多次的修订，事实证明如何对数据进行编码非常重要。 我的第一个编码存储了版本出现的每个修订版。

虽然很简单，但对于这些 JSON 文件的大小来说却是一场灾难。 正如您所期望的，大多数软件包的大多数版本在许多修订中都没有变化。 versions.json 文件的大小随着修订次数线性增长。

通过仅存储发布版本的最新修订版，我们可以保持文件较小，并且仍然回答“哪个修订版有此版本”的问题。 以下是随着修订被编入索引，它实际上是如何增长的：

5.18 MB，涵盖 1,393 个修订和 289,521 个不同的（属性、版本）对。

§Performance

我们的薄片的关键设计规则：

成本是按每个修订版计算的，而不是按每个包计算的。

如果我们添加修订作为输入，评估我们的薄片将会爆炸。 下面我们测量中的每个薄片都有 N nixpkgs 个输入和一个仅引用第一个的输出；时间是在该输出评估之前多长时间。44一切都是针对本地克隆的 git+file，因此没有网络延迟。

在输出评估之前，未使用的 5 个 nixpkgs 引脚将花费 26 秒。 每个输入大约需要 5 秒，即使从未使用过输入也会被获取并具体化。 相比之下，绿线是 nixpkgs-multiverse，有 1,393 个可用修订版，解析 JSON 的时间为 0.20 秒。 🤩

修订版本会被记忆，因此从一个修订版本中提取 3 个软件包的成本与提取 1 个软件包的成本相同。

§为什么我喜欢这个

/nix/store 可以保存同一包的许多图的概念是理解 Nix 的核心。 薄片的流行和兴起使得我们可以将 Nixpkg 的多个版本混合在一起变得更加明显。

我不断回想起 Nixpkg 的历史已经是多元宇宙了。 曾经存在的每个版本都已经构建、已经缓存、已经可以访问。 它只是通过提交哈希而不是版本号来解决，这与任何人的想法完全相反。

整个项目有 5 MB 的 JSON 和大约 200 行 Nix。 它不构建任何东西、镜像任何东西或托管任何东西。 这是一本电话簿。

inputs.multiverse.url = "github:fzakaria/nixpkgs-multiverse";
